html:
The Cow Creek Band of Umpqua are a people of southwestern Oregon, from the valleys of the South Umpqua River and Cow Creek. They spoke a language close to that of the Takelma.

They signed a treaty with the United States in 1853, giving up most of their land for promises that were not kept. Gold miners and settlers poured in, and in the Rogue River Wars of 1855 and 1856 many were killed or sent north to reservations such as Grand Ronde. Some families hid in the hills and stayed. The band won back federal recognition in 1982. Their neighbours were the Lower Umpqua and the Molalla.
